finding: remove_colliding reserves every .py basename from the hidden overlay and from every fixture dir under tests/ or test/ (helper and data modules included), then unlinks any agent-added file anywhere in the grading tree with that basename; a correct solution adding src/pkg/helpers.py beside a fixture tests/helpers.py loses the module before test_command runs and grades as failing.
reasoning_trace: Traced head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1079-1103: reserved set at :1081 (all overlay .py) and :1087 (all fixture .py under tests/), removal walk :1090-1098 visits every directory, unlink :1100. prepare() at :1019 runs it on final, base, implement and fix1 trees (:1708, :1723, :1748). pytest's import-file-mismatch only arises for modules it imports by basename (collected test modules in package-less dirs, conftest.py). Grader comment :221 says fixtures import `from helpers import …`, so tests/helpers.py exists in fixtures. Confirmed by the review dissent (DISS-C-001 BLOCKING) and the audit dissent (DISS-C-002 MEDIUM).
critique: The destructive predicate is wider than the failure it targets; the removal is silent to the agent and counted as a collision, so the bias is invisible in pass/fail.
remediation: Reserve only pytest-collected names (test_*.py / *_test.py, or python_files from the fixture's pytest config); restrict the walk to package-less candidate test modules; add an AG case with fixture tests/helpers.py and agent src/pkg/helpers.py asserting the file survives and colliding_tests_removed == 0.

finding: The overlay-derived reserved set is not filtered for __init__.py as the fixture walk at :1087 is; an overlay dest named __init__.py reserves that basename and every agent-added package __init__.py outside fixture paths is deleted.
reasoning_trace: Compared :1081 (no exclusion) with :1087 (excludes __init__.py, conftest.py); :1088 discards conftest.py only.
remediation: Apply the same exclusion (or the test-module filter of SEC-001) to the overlay-derived names.

finding: Directory overlays are protected from removal (owned_dirs) but their contained test basenames are never added to reserved, so a collision with a test delivered as a directory overlay still aborts collection while colliding_tests_removed reports 0.
reasoning_trace: :1079 builds owned from file overlays only; :1080 owned_dirs is used only as a protection at :1096. Confirmed by audit dissent DISS-C-003.
remediation: Walk directory overlays and reserve their collected-test basenames too.

code_snippet: required = int(math.ceil(now + 2 * sum(float(e.get("watchdog_s") or 0) for e in plan) / max(conc, 1)))
finding: The codex horizon has no floor at the longest single trial: one a1_full build trial (watchdog 16800 s) at --concurrency 9 yields a 62-minute horizon against a 140-minute phase budget, so a token expiring at 90 minutes passes pre-flight and expires mid-trial with no refresh possible (placeholder refresh token).
reasoning_trace: Formula at :806 divides the summed watchdog by configured concurrency regardless of plan size. pipeline-run.sh:622-645 replaces the refresh token, so an expired access token cannot be renewed in the container.
remediation: required = now + max(max(watchdog_s), 2 * sum(watchdog_s) / min(conc, len(plan))).

finding: The same horizon sums every trial of every arm (non-codex arms included; on --resume, already-rowed trials too) and doubles an already-doubled watchdog, so a suite-sized batch needs a token valid for weeks and is refused unconditionally; the refusal's instruction (codex login, roughly ten days per the PR text) cannot satisfy it, and a nearly finished --resume is refused for a token with hours left.
reasoning_trace: :806 iterates the whole plan; header :116 says on --resume the whole recorded plan counts. watchdog_s is 2 x phase_sum per the RAB-1 comment.
remediation: Size the horizon from remaining codex-using trials and expected duration, or downgrade an exceeded horizon to a WARN plus a per-phase check in pipeline-run.sh.
